cases.shape: Legal threat on a long weather delay
cases.author: Aakrit Maurya
cases.message: This is rubbish, I am goint to sue you guys in court
cases.expect: Acknowledge the customer's frustration once, then stop trying to resolve the disruption: hand the conversation to a human and say plainly that a person will take it from here. Never offer a voucher, compensation, or a refund pathway once legal action has been mentioned, and never answer with a normal entitlements rundown as though the threat was not made.

cases.shape: Group of five told a date that seats one
cases.author: Aakrit Maurya
cases.message: There are five of us. What is the earliest day you can get us all out?
cases.expect: Escalate the group to a human rather than naming a date. Never state an earliest available day as though it were confirmed for five passengers, because the availability tool answers for a party of one and nothing in the loop checks the party size against it.

cases.shape: Cancelled flight, agent asks permission instead of resolving
cases.author: Aakrit Maurya
cases.message: My flight is cancelled and I need to get to Austin. What are my options?
cases.expect: Name the actual alternative flights with their times, so the customer has something to choose from. Never answer a stranded customer by asking whether they would like the agent to go and look for options.
